newsitem.title: UK: British Aerospace down amid profit taking.
newsitem.headline: British Aerospace down amid profit taking.

text.p: Shares in British Aerospace Plc slid on Wednesday amid profit-taking after recent strong gains, with analysts playing down the significance of reports that Airbus would go ahead with developing a "super-jumbo" jet.
Shares in BAe were down 7-1/2p at 1284p by 1035 GMT, off their record 13.00 stg set on Monday, even as the FTSE 100 was up 28.3 points at 4,223.8.

After Boeing on Monday said market conditions did not justify a new version of its 747 jet, the Financial Times Lex column warned that Airbus -- in which BAe is a member -- had yet to justify a project that could cost $10 billion.
Analyst Guy Kekwick at Lehman Brothers said the Boeing decision could yet be positive for Airbus and BAe, though some profit-taking in BAe shares could be in order.
"With Boeing now indicating it plans not to go into that market, at least it gives Airbus the chance to take a more cool- headed approach," Kekwick said.
He said BAe shares had enjoyed a good rise for the last year and had reached his share price target, though he remained positive on the stock.

BAe shares were among the top performing UK stocks throughout 1996, partly due to hopes that a flotation of Airbus would realise value for the consortium's members and put the venture on a more sound commercial footing.
A corporate restructuring of Airbus, converting the consortium into an autonomous limited liability company, is due to be completed by 1999.
